clauses.reason: Section 1 closes executive branch departments and agencies and excuses their employees from duty for the last half of the scheduled workday on Tuesday, December 24, 2002. It operates only on that day and has no application after it. The first end is that day, 2002-12-24, recorded inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, that the command ends when that day begins, is the alternative. The order states no earlier end, and no held later instrument revokes, supersedes or amends it.

Section 2 lets agency heads determine that certain offices, installations and employees must remain open and on duty for the full scheduled workday on December 24, 2002. It operates only on that day and has no application after it. The first end is that day, 2002-12-24, recorded inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, that the command ends when that day begins, is the alternative. The order states no earlier end, and no held later instrument revokes, supersedes or amends it.

Section 3 treats Tuesday, December 24, 2002 as within the scope of EO 11582 and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) and similar statutes for pay and leave. It operates only on that day and has no application after it. The first end is that day, 2002-12-24, recorded inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, that the command ends when that day begins, is the alternative. The order states no earlier end, and no held later instrument revokes, supersedes or amends it.

research_rationale:
EO 13281 (signed 2002-12-19; 67 FR 78319, Federal Register of 2002-12-23, FR Doc. 02-32518) was read in full in the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13281.txt. Identity: number, date and subject (Half-Day Closing of Executive Departments and Agencies of the Federal Government on Tuesday, December 24, 2002) agree with the census register row (2002-12-19). Section 1 closes executive branch departments and agencies and excuses their employees from duty for the last half of the scheduled workday on Tuesday, December 24, 2002, except as section 2 provides; section 2 lets agency heads determine that certain offices, installations and employees must remain open and on duty for the full scheduled workday on December 24, 2002 for reasons of national security or defense or other public reasons; section 3 treats December 24, 2002 as within the scope of EO 11582 of February 11, 1971 and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) and similar statutes for pay and leave. Every command is tied to that single day, so each clause ends by its own terms on 2002-12-24, recorded inclusive as the owner's until-date ruling (2026-10-21) directs; the exclusive reading (the commands end when that day begins) is the alternative a reviewer should see. Searches: a by-number search of the held order texts for EO 13281 finds only this order's own Federal Register text (one match in one file), and the three machine searches record no later amendment, revocation or supersession (current-law:usc 0, current-law:ecfr 0, later-events:ofr_catalog 0); the later-events edge file holds no edge for this order and the catalog row carries no disposition note. EO 11582, which section 3 cites, was signed in 1971 and is not a later instrument. The held text is the machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF; the PDF page images are not held, so identity (printed number, title, signing date and FR Doc. number) was checked on the text layer against the census register row.

savings.reason: Employees excused from duty on the named day were excused under the order, and pay and leave for that day are governed by EO 11582 and the cited statutes, which the order only applied to the day; those accrued pay and leave effects rest on the cited authorities and do not keep the order operative after 2002-12-24.
